key_idea: Compare the numbers twice: as (int, frac-as-integer) tuples and as true decimals with the fraction right-padded to 5 digits; print the larger only if both comparisons agree.
sketch: Split each string at the dot. For the tuple comparison parse the fractional digits as an integer (leading zeros vanish). For the real comparison right-pad the fractional digits with zeros to length 5 and compare lexicographically as integers. If the two sign results differ (including the tuple comparison being a tie, e.g. 4.1 vs 4.01), output -1; otherwise output the larger number exactly as it was given. O(1). Pitfall: avoid floating point and print the original string, not a reformatted number.
